key_insight: SELECTBENCH shows that current generative structure-based drug design models offer only modest discrimination between target and off-target proteins.
clinical_relevance: Better molecular selectivity could support safer drug discovery, including oncology, but this study does not establish clinical safety or cancer-specific benefit.
method: Introduce SELECTBENCH to evaluate molecular selectivity.
Assess literature cases, pharmaceutical safety panels, and large-scale protein-structure sets.
Compare nine models, including selectivity-trained methods and inference-time guidance.
evidence_signal: Across three evaluation tasks, selectivity-trained models showed modest off-target discrimination, while inference-time guidance provided limited gains.
watch_item: Computational selectivity results require experimental validation and cannot rule out unknown off-target interactions.
paper_title: On the Selectivity of Generative Models in Structure-Based Drug Design
